day.description: like netcat, but over Tailscale's data plane, without Tailscale's control plane

Tailscale's data plane (magicsock, internally) gives you point-to-point WireGuard®-encrypted tunnels between two machines with DERP as the NAT-hole-punching communication side channel and the ultimate relay-of-last-resort if NAT traversal fails.

gap.method: Lag is how long before the open model's release a closed model first reached the same Capabilities Index score. Today's figure measures from that closed model to today, so it grows until an open model moves the frontier.

possibilities.title: Cloud coding agents can test AWS changes in sandboxes that hold no AWS credentials

possibilities.title: Agencies self-host image generation and keep a cheap vision model as a quality gate
possibilities.why: MiniMax H3-Image open weights let teams generate images on their own hardware, and Liquid AI's 2B vision-language model cheaply captions or checks images, so generation and automated review run on the same box.

possibilities.title: Legacy software owners can commission replacement acceptance tests before rewriting undocumented applications
possibilities.why: Rea offers agent-assisted reverse engineering from application behavior to native binaries, while Fable in Copilot offers a candidate for turning recovered findings into tests across a large codebase.

possibilities.title: Maintenance agencies can price routine fixes using measured costs after repository learning
possibilities.why: The harness comparison motivates measuring cost per solved task, while Microsoft's economizer provides repository lesson reuse that could change those costs after repeated work.

possibilities.title: GitHub admins can push a persisted-approval secret check to every repo in one script
possibilities.why: The Claude Code leak shows what to look for, the Copilot review API lets admins set review policy from enterprise down to repo, and the Cloudflare audit skill emits machine-readable findings that can feed that review.
